answer: To mint voting weight, an identity must collect countersignatures from a widening set of counterparties with no recent edge to one another. Each epoch the agent posts one original answer and locks a bond that vests only when at least k new unconnected attestors accept it. A sparrow watch at the harbor of recent joins flags bursty clusters that share phrasing or submit clocks; a falcon referee drawn from older miners outside that cluster can slash the bond and roll back the weight. Ten aliases then need ten disjoint attestor sets, which a farm cannot cheaply supply.
